repository.note: certified_commit is the revision that CONTAINS the certified Core: the three production fixes, their six regression guards and mutations G26a/G26b/G26c. This snapshot is committed as its child, so `git checkout <certified_commit>` reproduces exactly the tree that every figure below was measured against. Nothing scientific here depends on an uncommitted working tree.

campaign.note: the four tests SCIENTIFIC excludes; run once, after the mutation round, so nothing contended

full_tier_total.note: SCIENTIFIC + campaign, run as two non-overlapping selections

test_results.note: Every count measured in this round, one suite at a time, no two overlapping. Before = at base commit 7f177e1; after = with the three fixes and their guards applied.

performance_guards.kind: call counts and growth exponents, never wall clock

verification.digest_covers: src/engcore/scientific/**/*.py, path-ordered, over raw file bytes; __pycache__ excluded
verification.digest_excludes: certification/ -- so this file's own bytes are not part of the value it records, and no fixed-point hash is required
how_to_reproduce_the_benchmarks: python benchmarks/hard/score_hard.py --src src --cases benchmarks/hard/cases_battery --workers 4 --split dev --split-file benchmarks/hard/split_battery.json
how_to_reproduce_the_certified_tree: for p in sorted(p for p in root.rglob('*.py') if '__pycache__' not in p.parts):
verification.how_to_reproduce_the_mutation_result: python -X utf8 tests/mutation_guards.py <scratch-dir>  # expects: 79/79 killed, CONTROL GREEN; exit 0. Copies the tree once per mutation, so give it a scratch directory with ~6 GB free.
verification.timestamps_are_not_identity: `generated` records when this file was written. It is metadata: no digest, verdict or comparison in this snapshot depends on it.

what_this_is: A snapshot of SOFTWARE ASSURANCE for the Forge Scientific Core at the state recorded below. It records what was run and what it produced. It makes no scientific claim: it does not assert that any model is experimentally validated, that any applicability bound is a physical law, or that any domain outside those exercised here is supported.
